title: Customer-facing status and closure note — severe degradation
body:
Purpose
This document is a customer-facing two-part artifact: 1) a concise status-page / email blurb to publish while an event is active, and 2) a short post-incident closure summary for customers once we've completed the internal review. The language below is intentionally non-technical where possible, and contains clear guidance for customers who may have been affected.

Use guidance
- Status page blurb should be posted verbatim to status.redwood.ai with any customer-specific substitution (region, model, route).
- The closure summary is suitable for the status page incident notes and for direct customer emails from CSMs or support leads.
- Keep all references to internal ticket numbers and debugging artifacts in linked_artifacts; do not include stack traces or sensitive logs in customer-facing copy.

A. Live status blurb (short — publish immediately)
Title: Degraded text-generation throughput in US-West — partial impact
Posted: 2026-10-04 18:12 UTC
Summary: We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent timeouts affecting text generation requests for some customers in the US-West region. Some requests returned slower responses or failed to complete. Our mitigation teams are actively working on a fix; traffic may be routed to alternate capacity while we stabilize.
Impact: Customers using hosted API endpoints in US-West may see increased per-request latency and a small number of request failures. Embeddings and read-only management APIs were unaffected.
What we are doing: We have identified a service component that is intermittently overloading GPU workers and are rolling a targeted process-level rollback and capacity rebalance. We will post updates every 30 minutes or sooner when there is a material change.
Customer guidance: If you are experiencing errors, retry with exponential backoff. If you rely on strict low latency SLOs we recommend switching to a pinned dedicated instance (if enrolled) or routing to another region as a temporary measure. For critical cases contact support with priority flag.
Next update: 2026-10-04 18:45 UTC

B. Expanded status update (30–90 minute follow-up)
Posted: 2026-10-04 18:45 UTC
Summary: Mitigation actions are in progress. We have rolled back a recent autoscaling optimization change in the serving runtime that correlated with the onset of increased load on worker processes. Early telemetry shows latency starting to return toward normal for most traffic, though a subset of long-sequence generation jobs remain affected.
Impact update: Approximately 8% of hosted API requests in the affected region experienced >2x latency during the peak; error rate peaked at ~0.9% for generation routes. No data loss reported; requests that failed typically returned 5xx errors.
What we are doing: Rolling rollback complete for 60% of traffic, performing slow ramp of the rollback for remaining workers, and temporarily increasing reserved capacity for the region. Teams are monitoring KV cache hit ratios and worker GC metrics.
Customer guidance: Continue to retry failed requests; if you see persistent failures include request IDs in your ticket.
Next update: 2026-10-04 19:30 UTC or sooner.

C. Customer-facing post-incident closure summary (publish once internal postmortem is final)
Posted: 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC
Root-cause (customer-facing, non-sensitive): The incident was caused by an autoscaling optimization that incorrectly targeted a narrow subset of GPU worker processes handling long-sequence text generation. Under a specific request pattern the optimization caused uneven task distribution which overloaded some workers and increased latency and failure rates.
Impact summary: Between 2026-10-04 17:58 UTC and 2026-10-04 20:22 UTC customers with hosted API routes in US-West experienced elevated latency and intermittent generation failures. Peak impact lasted ~45 minutes. No customer data was lost and management/metadata APIs were not affected.
Actions taken during incident:
- Immediate rollback of the autoscaling optimization that correlated with the behavior.
- Temporary capacity increase in US-West to absorb backlog.
- Rate-of-change guardrails added to the autoscaling pipeline to prevent aggressive changes during steady-state load.
Remediation and long-term prevention for customers:
- We have disabled the problematic optimization and implemented a safer, staged rollout for future autoscaling changes.
- New telemetry and alerting rules have been added for worker imbalance metrics and long-sequence job latency.
- We will run a dedicated test-matrix covering the long-sequence generation patterns in pre-prod prior to future autoscaling releases.
Customer impact mitigation options available now:
- Customers on hosted plans: If you were materially affected and require credit consideration, open a support case with "INC-2026-10-04-DEG-47 - Credit" and include primary tester route(s) and representative request IDs. Our support team will review and respond within standard SLA windows.
- Dedicated/private customers: Contact your TAM or platform engineer for region-level options and reroute guidance.
Follow-up commitments:
- Post-incident internal review scheduled: 2026-10-07 11:00 UTC; summary blog (internal) and action items to be completed within 4 weeks.
- A customer-facing technical appendix with additional telemetry graphs and a non-sensitive timeline will be posted to the incident page at status.redwood.ai when available.

D. Suggested email to affected customers (CSM / Support template)
Subject: Update on US-West generation degradation (Oct 4) — summary and next steps
Hi <Customer Name>,

We want to follow up on the service degradation you may have seen on Oct 4 in US‑West. Our teams identified the cause and have completed mitigations; most customers returned to normal operation within an hour. We’re sorry for the disruption.

What happened: A recent autoscaling optimization caused worker unevenness under a particular workload pattern which led to higher latency and some failed generation requests.
What we did: rolled back the optimization, increased region capacity, and put additional guardrails in place.
What this means for you: No data was lost. If you experienced increased error rates and would like us to investigate specific requests, please reply with request IDs or open a support case and reference INC-2026-10-04-DEG-47. If you want to explore options to reduce exposure to regional degradation, we can discuss Dedicated routing or multi-region routing strategies.
Compensation: If your account was materially impacted, contact support to request a credit review.
Contact escalation: Your CSM is <CSM Name> and the on-call SRE handling this incident is <SRE Name>. If you need immediate assistance, escalate with priority flag in the support portal.

E. Short FAQ (for CSMs to copy-paste)
Q: Did Redwood expose any customer data?
A: No — this incident only affected request latency and failures; no customer data was exfiltrated or lost.

Q: Which APIs were impacted?
A: Text generation routes in US-West for hosted API customers. Embeddings and on-prem/private control planes were not affected.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We have implemented technical and process changes to reduce the risk, including disabling the change that caused the incident, adding targeted telemetry, and performing an expanded pre-production test matrix.

F. Internal notes for reviewers (do not publish)
- Keep an audit log of which customers received the email and whether they requested credits.
- Link internal postmortem DOC: CONFLUENCE-1234.
- Owner for follow-up remediation tasks: eng-serving-runtime / Maria Patel.

G. Quick publishing checklist
- Verify timestamp/timezone in the status page UI.
- Replace placeholders (<Customer Name>, <CSM Name>, <SRE Name>) before sending customer emails.
- Do not include sensitive logs.
- Attach the incident status URL and a short timeline to customer notes.

If you have edits to the text above or alternative phrasing you prefer for a specific customer, add comments below or ping the CSM channel (#cs-customer-communications).
